the same command through its HTTP binding

facts.Rayfold: yes: both commands replay their original results

methods.title: Replace
methods.operation: Editor A replaces review r2. Editor B, still holding the previous version, replaces it too.

request.body: {"query":"mutation($id: ID!, $rating: Int!, $body: String!) { editReview(id: $id, rating: $rating, body: $body) { id rating body } }","variables":{"id":"r2","rating":5,"body":"Reread it: better than I remembered."}}
{"query":"mutation($id: ID!, $rating: Int!, $body: String!) { editReview(id: $id, rating: $rating, body: $body) { id rating body } }","variables":{"id":"r2","rating":2,"body":"Too slow for me."}}

GraphQL.label: editor B, stale: accepted, A's edit is gone

facts.metric: fields not sent are left untouched

facts.metric: open views correct without a refetch (catalogue + product page)
facts.REST: 1 of 2: the PATCH response replaces the page; the list is stale
facts.GraphQL: 2 of 2: the normalized cache merges the returned book

facts.metric: another user's open view updates by itself

facts.metric: validation rule and published contract come from one source

methods.title: Delete
methods.operation: The author deletes review r2 while the book page (which lists it) is cached. Then the client retries, as it does when a response is lost.

Rayfold.label: retry after a lost response: replayed

facts.metric: cached views still showing the deleted review
facts.REST: 1: the cached list keeps it until a refetch
facts.GraphQL: 1: a normalized cache does not remove deleted entities from lists by itself
facts.Rayfold: 0: the command's { "del": "Review:r2" } patch removes it everywhere

facts.metric: a retry after a lost response reports the original success
facts.REST: no: 404, indistinguishable from a wrong id
facts.Rayfold: yes: the idempotency key replays the first result
